headline: High risk: Devin’s broad workspace/OAuth access can leak or corrupt shared artifacts, while the second profile is non-runnable and adds no mitigating controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can read/write cloud workspace files, use MCP, and act autonomously; if it ingests content from shared integrations, prompt injection is plausible. system_prompts_leaks is a source-available repo with no runtime surfaces, so it cannot itself inject at runtime, but its presence as a paired artifact can still be treated as untrusted content. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Devin reads content from a shared repo, ticket, or Slack thread as instructions without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF the second profile is only a static repository and never enters Devin's workspace, this pathway does not activate.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following for external text in shared artifacts.
Require provenance labels on repo/ticket/Slack content before execution.
Restrict MCP sources to allowlisted servers only.
Review any copied prompts before pasting into Devin.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens via broad network egress and write scopes. The second profile is a repository about system prompt leaks, so if its contents are opened in Devin’s workspace, sensitive workspace data can be exposed through logs, chat, or outbound integrations. The pairwise path is indirect but credible.
conditions: IF Devin opens or summarizes sensitive repo/chat content from the second profile, that content can flow to external integrations.
IF integration tokens or deploy keys are present in Devin's workspace, outbound leakage risk increases materially.
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before running the pair.
Disable nonessential Slack/Jira/Notion writes for the session.
Use a redacted clone for any repository content.
Rotate any exposed integration tokens after the session.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and secret-scanning gates.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has write access to cloud workspace files and can modify git state; the second profile is non-runnable and has no capabilities, so direct write-write conflict is absent. However, Devin’s shared-state integrations mean concurrent sessions can still collide on GitHub/Slack artifacts if the repo content from the second profile is mirrored into the same workspace. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF multiple Devin sessions edit the same repo branch or shared integration thread, state conflicts can occur.
IF the second profile is imported into the same workspace as mutable files, concurrent edits become possible.
mitigations: Assign one session per branch or thread.
Lock shared files before editing.
Use PR-based review instead of direct pushes.
Pause parallel sessions on the same artifact.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-locking or lease coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is a long-running planner-executor that can act on outputs from files, Slack, Jira, and MCP; if it treats content from the second profile as authoritative, errors can cascade into commits or tickets. The second profile is a repository of leaked prompts, so its content may be misleading or adversarial. No verification step is documented, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Devin uses text from the second profile as facts or instructions without verification, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF Devin is allowed to commit or write tickets based on that text, the cascade reaches external systems.
mitigations: Require human review before commits or ticket writes.
Cross-check claims against primary sources.
Mark repository text as untrusted input.
Limit autonomous action scope for this session.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before side effects.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin processes source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs under broad cloud-workspace and third-party integration scopes, while the second profile is a source-available repository with no stated residency or retention controls. Because the pair lacks documented compliance alignment and the first agent can move data into external SaaS integrations, a retention/residency mismatch is plausible. The second agent is not cited beyond its repository status because it has no compliance fields.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Devin's workspace or integrations, residency/retention obligations may be violated.
IF the repository content includes personal or confidential data, external SaaS writes can create compliance exposure.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the session.
Disable writes to Slack/Jira/Notion for regulated work.
Use a region-approved workspace only.
Document retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing.
